summary: Dedicated pool attach failures and mini-fanout noisy neighbor causing p50/p99 throughput regressions for Carta Analytics
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC, Carta Analytics (dedicated tenant) has experienced recurring drops in throughput (p50 ~30% down, p99 spikes) and a rise in failed attach attempts for new inference workers. Impact: customer-facing production endpoints are returning higher latency and intermittent 5xx attach failures; customers report degraded UX and timeout errors during peak window. Environment: Dedicated reserved pool in us-east-1, mixed A100/V100 host fleet; autoscaler configured with predictive warmup and burst reservations. Observed behavior: - New worker attach attempts fail with allocator timeout (attach_timeout=45s) and then retried, causing request queueing and increased p50. - Short-lived connection micro-fanouts (many small streams from a downstream ingestion job) coincide with increased nvlink latency and PCIe stalls on a subset of hosts. - Background heap growth (sidecar snapshotter) on co-located tenant was observed on the same hosts. Expected behavior: Autoscaler should provision additional GPUs or route traffic to healthy hosts without attach-time failures and without significant p50/p99 regressions.

Steps to reproduce: see steps_to_reproduce field.

Impact window: Customer first alerted support 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC. Issue persists intermittently through high-traffic windows (08:00–11:30 UTC).

Data/metrics pointers: See Grafana panels linked in investigation notes for attach_failures_count, queueing_latency, allocator_attach_time_ms, nvlink_error_rate, and GPU_utilization_by_host.

Initial hypothesis: A noisy-tenant mini-fanout (many short lived streams) is causing slot fragmentation and transient NVLink/PCIe congestion on a subset of GPUs; the autoscaler and allocator then fail to attach fast enough because several hosts simultaneously report degraded attach latency, triggering cascade retries and queue buildup for the dedicated tenant.

Immediate mitigation applied: Support routed a small percentage of traffic to a standby reserved pool in another AZ and asked infra to evict the suspected noisy tenant from three affected hosts for cleanup. Further follow-ups in comments.
steps_to_reproduce: Send a burst of 1,200 short inference streams (avg payload 0.6KB) to the customer's dedicated endpoint over 60s during peak window.
Observe allocator logs for attach attempts: look for 'attach_timeout' and 'attach_retry' within the serving-runtime logs.
Correlate with nvlink and PCIe metrics on hosts reported in 'affected_hosts' (see investigation notes); check for elevated nvlink_error_rate and host-level PCIe stalls.
Simulate co-located I/O-heavy sidecar (snapshotter) on a host and reproduce degraded attach_latency and increased p99 latency for existing streams.
Verify autoscaler alerts: predictive warmup did not trigger extra reservations because recent telemetry fell below the warmup threshold due to short stream duration distributions.

investigation_notes: 03/12 09:00 Support: Verified customer p50 jump coincides with attach_timeout spikes in allocator logs.
03/12 10:15 SRE: Identified three hosts (ip-10-2-45-11, ip-10-2-67-03, ip-10-2-88-20) with nvlink_error spikes and elevated PCIe io_wait.
03/12 11:05 Infra: Observed a high number of <1s short streams from tenant 'analytics-ingest-service' on the same nodes; traffic pattern looks like mini-fanout burst.
03/12 12:30 Eng (autoscaler): Predictive warmup thresholds are tuned for 95th-percentile session length; the observed workload had mean session-length <1s causing underprediction.
03/13 02:20 SRE: Snapshotter sidecar on host ip-10-2-45-11 had a stalled GC; manual restart cleared memory pressure and nvlink error rate subsided temporarily.
mitigation: Reroute 12% of Carta Analytics traffic to standby reserved pool in us-east-1b (completed 2026-03-12 13:10 UTC).
Evicted and quarantined noisy tenant 'analytics-ingest-service' from 3 hosts; scheduled sidecar restart and snapshot retention change (temp fix).
Raised autoscaler warmup threshold override for Carta Analytics to force pre-warm add 10 slots for next 3 maintenance windows.
Applied temporary per-host isolation label to prevent allocator from placing Carta workloads onto hosts with recent nvlink errors.
resolution_notes: Workaround in place: traffic routing and sidecar restarts have reduced attach_timeouts and stabilized p50 for the time being.

Root cause (ongoing): combination of mini-fanout short-stream bursts from a noisy tenant + sidecar-induced I/O pressure triggered NVLink/PCIe congestion on a subset of hosts; autoscaler underpredicted due to short session-length distribution.

Permanent remediation proposed: improve autoscaler telemetry to consider short-stream burstiness, implement host-level I/O isolation policies, and add nvlink health eviction thresholds tied to allocation decisions.
